chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Harun ibn Kharjah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Salat is assigned to an angel who has no other work besides it. So when one finishes from it, he captures it, then ascends with it. So if it was from what is accepted, it is accepted, and if it was from what is not accepted, it is said to him: 'Return it to My servant.' So he descends with it until he strikes it upon his face, then he says: 'Uff to you! You do not cease to produce deeds that tire Me.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to rejected prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the metaphysical journey of Salat, where a dedicated angel acts as the intermediary between the worshipper and the Divine Presence. The rejection mechanism—where the angel strikes the prayer against the worshipper's face—serves as a tangible sign of spiritual negligence, emphasizing that mere ritual performance without presence of heart may result in the prayer being returned rather than ascended.
